reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The reading assumes stored verifier findings already have a resolved state. They do not (records.rs:750 Finding has severity, summary, evidence, location and source only), so the 'unresolved' half of the request has no defined meaning in the current data. (round 1 of 3). I checked the plan against the snapshot with Read and Grep; I ran nothing. The plan is well placed: the retry findings go into the producer brief at the point where unseeded retries lose them today; the post-mortem part extends the existing introspection record; and the D130, CHANGELOG and records.md edits match the request. Two design problems remain. First, it claims the third Jev question can fail on its own. In fact the real client's `parse_response` rejects the whole reply when any answer is missing, so the new question can wipe out the class and repeat answers in production. The FakeJev-based tests would not catch this. Second, the 'resolved' state the plan filters on does not exist and nothing would ever set it, so 'resolved findings are left out' is shown only on hand-made data. The planner can fix both, so the verdict is revise. Findings: minor: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (files, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs); minor: crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs is not among the reading's deliverables (files, crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs); major: The claim that the class and repeat answers are read independently of the new question is false for the real Jev client. (Decision 4 and Risks (FakeJev answers); crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs:147-170); major: No stored finding has a resolved state. The plan adds a `resolved` flag that nothing ever sets, so 'resolved ones left out' is shown only on hand-made data and never happens in a real run. (Decision 1 and Open question 1; Demonstration for criterion 1); minor: A seeded retry's Retry section lists every finding, minor ones included, while the new section lists only blocker and major findings. The two paths describe 'the previous attempt's findings' differently. (Decision 2 (seeded case))
